name: Contrue Fonte
tagline: Paid font duo that pairs a clean sans serif with a blackletter display style, plus a blur style
description:
Contrue Fonte is a font duo by Jolicia Type, sold on the Marketore marketplace. It pairs a plain contemporary sans serif with a dramatic blackletter style. The seller aims it at headlines, posters, album covers, branding and editorial work.

The duo also includes a blur style for experimental layouts. The listing gives OTF, TTF and web font files in a ZIP download. It does not state a glyph count, the language support or the number of weights.

The product page shows 13 preview images and has no reviews and no comments. Jolicia Type sells other display fonts in the same shop.
pricing_detail: Personal licence $23, Commercial licence $25 and Extended licence $1,200, each a one-time purchase. The purchase includes a ZIP file, instant download, lifetime re-downloads and 14-day buyer protection.
agent_guidance:
Read the product page for the licence tiers and the file formats. The page lists OTF, TTF and Web Font.

The listing does not state language support or a glyph count, so do not assume extended Latin. Use the face for headlines and display text only, and buy the Commercial or Extended licence before you use it in client work.
why_it_matters: It gives a sans and blackletter pairing in one purchase, with a blur style for poster and music work.
tier_reason: A clear three-tier licence and OTF, TTF and web font files. Held at C because the page gives no glyph count, no language support and no specimen text, and the product has 0 reviews.

name: Aratana
tagline: Grotesque Latin typeface by Arata Nagara, in private beta with a live specimen and a PDF
description:
Aratana is a Latin grotesque typeface by Arata Nagara, a manga artist and designer based in Tokyo. He describes it as a Helvetica alternative with a sense of speed. He based it on Radim Peško's Specta and on Bricolage Grotesque.

The specimen page lists 4 weights from ExtraLight to Bold, a variable weight axis from 200 to 700, 352 glyphs with extended Latin, kerning and f-ligatures. It names OTF, TTF and WOFF2 formats. A type tester, the character set, detail notes and a PDF specimen are on the page.

The font is not on general release. The Japanese text says he looks for beta testers among people who know him. The page has no download, no price and no licence.
pricing_detail: No price and no licence on the page. The font is in a private beta for people the designer knows.
agent_guidance:
Read the specimen page and the PDF specimen for the glyph set and the weights. You cannot download or license the font from the page.

Do not use it in a build. Suggest it only as a reference, and send the user to the designer's contact link to ask about access.
why_it_matters: It is a documented grotesque with a variable axis and a full specimen. It is useful as a reference for fast, neutral Latin type.
tier_reason: A full live specimen with 352 glyphs, a variable axis and a PDF. Held at C because the font is not available: there is no download, no price and no licence, and the beta is open only to people the designer knows.
notable_for: 4 weights plus a 200 to 700 variable axis

name: Allo
tagline: Free OFL variable sans with weight, roundness and optical size axes, true obliques and icons
description:
Allo is a free, open source font family by Josh Puckett. His portfolio has its own record in this catalog under the slug josh-puckett. Allo started from Inter 4.1, and every glyph is redrawn.

The family has three variable axes: weight from 100 to 900, roundness from 0 to 100, and optical size from 14 to 32. It has a drawn oblique in every weight, 606 glyphs, support for 50+ languages, tabular figures, fractions, stylistic sets and character variants. It also has icon glyphs and arrows that form when you type them.

The site has a type tester, an OpenType feature tester and a poster maker. You get the font as a ZIP, from npm as allo-font, or from the GitHub repository.
pricing_detail: Free under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. The site shows a price of $0.00. You can use it in commercial work, but you cannot sell the font files on their own.
agent_guidance:
Install the web fonts with npm i allo-font, or download https://allo.joshpuckett.me/downloads/Allo-1.0.3.zip for desktop files. Read /llms.txt for the licence summary and the download contents.

Set the wght, ROND and opsz axes with font-variation-settings. Keep OFL.txt with the font files, and credit it as "Allo by Josh Puckett".
why_it_matters: It is a free UI sans with a roundness axis and automatic optical size, so one family covers text and display sizes.
tier_reason: OFL licence, 1,545 GitHub stars, an npm package, 606 glyphs, three variable axes and an llms.txt. Held below S because version 1.0.3 is from 2026 with a short track record, and it covers Latin script only.

name: Kinetik
tagline: Animated React components on Tailwind CSS and Motion, installed with the shadcn CLI
description:
Kinetik is a library of animated React components by Gourav Singh, built with Tailwind CSS and Motion. You do not install it as a package. The shadcn CLI copies each component into your project, with its npm packages and design tokens.

The library has 28 free components under MIT and 6 Pro components. Groups are Buttons, Animations, Data, Effects, Inputs, Layout, Media, Navigation and Scenes. Examples are a folder that fans out its papers, a fire and smoke glow, a chrome send button, a menubar, a command palette and AI parts such as streaming messages, citations and tool calls.

Each component page has a live preview, the source and its variants. The free source is on GitHub.
pricing_detail: 28 components are free under MIT. 6 Pro components cost $8 once, and the Pro licence allows commercial use but forbids resale or a competing library. Refunds only for double charges or failed unlocks, within 14 days.
agent_guidance:
Read /llms.txt for the list of components and their docs URLs. Install one with npx shadcn@latest add https://kinetikui.singhgourav.site/r/<name>.json, and get the index at /r/registry.json.

The CLI adds the npm packages and design tokens the component needs. Pro components need a personal install command from a paid account, so use only the free ones unless the user has Pro.
why_it_matters: It gives shadcn-installable motion pieces, including AI answer parts, that land in the repo as editable source.
tier_reason: 28 MIT components with a shadcn registry, live previews and an llms.txt. Held at B because the repository is about six weeks old with 13 stars, GitHub reports no detected licence file, and one person maintains it.
notable_for: built on Tailwind CSS and Motion

name: Uizze
tagline: Free anti UI-slop agent skills, plus a paid MCP of real web and iOS screens
description:
Uizze gives coding agents design guidance and real app references, so the UI they build looks less generic. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot. Objective Company makes it.

The free part is two agent skills under MIT: ui-design for design and redesign work, and anti-ui-slop for a finish pass on agent-made UI. You install them with the skills CLI or as a Claude Code plugin. The site also has guides, a coding-agent UI checklist and a GitHub Action for pull requests.

The paid part is a hosted MCP server with three tools: find_ui_references, find_ui_materials and get_ui_flow. The llms.txt claims 800,000+ real web and iOS screens. The MCP needs full access and an agent token.
pricing_detail: The skills are free. Full access with the MCP costs $9 a month or $85 a year. The pricing page shows $199 one-time for lifetime, but its meta description says $169.

Install the free skill with npx skills add https://uizze.com --skill anti-ui-slop, or ui-design for wider design work. Read https://uizze.com/llms.txt first for the install commands and the agent rules.

The skills work without an account. Use the hosted MCP at https://uizze.com/mcp only with a user-supplied token, sent as an HTTP bearer header. Do not copy branding, copy text or exact layouts from the references.

name: ThinkUI
tagline: Paid hosted MCP server that returns real UI screens, components, animated icons and fonts with sources
description:
ThinkUI is a hosted MCP server that gives coding agents interface references from shipped products. Each result names its source product, its capture date and its licence. It works with Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed, Codex and ChatGPT connectors.

The server has five tools: find_ui_references, find_ui_elements, find_animated_icons, find_ui_materials and corpus_stats. The homepage counts 1,565 screenshots from 277 products, 3,802 HTML and CSS components, 1,698 animated SVG icons, 1,114 written references and 119 fonts, icon sets and systems. Components and icons are MIT. Only 428 screenshots are permissively licensed, and the rest are marked study-only.

A companion skill and an anti-slop finish gate install with the skills CLI. When the library has no match, the server returns an empty result and lists what it does hold.
pricing_detail: Starter $7.99 a month and Pro $15.99 a month on a 20% sale (list $9.99 and $19.99), each with a 3-day trial that needs a card. Lifetime is $152 once (list $190), with no trial. The llms.txt still lists the full prices.
agent_guidance:
Add {"url": "https://thinkui.xyz/mcp"} to the MCP config with an Authorization: Bearer header, or use OAuth. Read https://thinkui.xyz/llms.txt for the tools and the auth flow.

Call corpus_stats first to see what the library holds. Ship only results marked MIT or permissive. Screenshots marked "do not ship or republish" are for study only.
why_it_matters: It gives an agent cited, licence-tagged UI references and pasteable parts, and it says when it has no match.
tier_reason: Five documented MCP tools, licence and source on every result, published library counts and an llms.txt with OAuth details. Held at B because there is no free tier, a trial needs a card, and most screenshots are study-only.

name: Taste Skill
tagline: MIT agent skill that gives coding agents an art direction, real photos and a browser check
description:
Taste Skill is an open source agent skill by Leon Lin, with the install name design-taste-frontend. It makes coding agents build company websites and app screens that look designed, not generated. It works in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and other agents that read SKILL.md files.

The skill is a folder of rules, reference files, a library of palettes, type pairings and hero layouts, and Node scripts. The scripts deal a direction, find openly licensed photos and credit them, and check the page in headless Chrome at several widths. A finish gate holds the build until no fixable failure is left, for three rounds at most.

It needs Node 22 or newer and Chrome, Edge or Chromium. It uses no API keys. Older skills from the repo now live in taste-skill-classics and imagegen-skills.
pricing_detail: Free and open source under MIT. GitHub sponsors and listed company sponsors support the project.
agent_guidance:
Install with npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend", or as a Claude Code plugin with /plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill. Read https://www.tasteskill.dev/llms.txt for the run steps.

Make sure that Node 22+ and a Chrome-family browser are present before a run. A full build takes 30 to 45 minutes and a few hundred thousand tokens, so do not start it for a small UI change.
why_it_matters: It is a widely used design skill against AI slop, and it checks its own output in a real browser before it hands the page over.

name: Refto
tagline: Curated website inspiration gallery, plus a Mac reference library with on-device AI search
description:
Refto has two parts. Explore is a free, curated website inspiration gallery with screenshots, version history and tags by category, style and section. It also has DESIGN.md examples, design topics, collections and a tools directory. Refto for Mac is a reference library app, and the homepage presents it.

The Mac app keeps images, videos, audio, PDFs and web pages on your Mac and finds them by what they show and say. The AI models run on the Mac, with no account and no uploads. A browser extension for Chrome, Edge, Arc, Brave and Safari saves from X, Pinterest, Dribbble, Behance and other sites. A local MCP server and a refto command let coding agents search and add to the library.

The app is in beta and needs macOS 15 and Apple silicon. ActNow makes it. The sitemap lists about 460 gallery site pages and 1,661 tool pages.
pricing_detail: The Explore gallery is free. The Mac app has a 15-day free trial, then a one-time licence: launch price $12.99 for 2 Macs or $16.99 for 3 Macs until version 1.0 (regular $18.99 and $24.99). Refunds within 14 days.

name: ASCII Playground
tagline: Andreas Gysin's live-code editor for text-mode art, with example sketches and open source
description:
ASCII Playground is a live-code environment for text-only output by Andreas Gysin (ertdfgcvb). A program is a JavaScript module whose main() function returns a character for each cell of a grid, the same way a fragment shader returns a color for each pixel.

The editor shows the output, the code and a menu side by side. It includes 47 example programs, from basics to demos, and you can open the source of each one in the editor. Helper modules give GLSL-style math, vectors, color palettes, text art blocks, draggable windows, image and camera input.

The core is open source under Apache-2.0 as ertdfgcvb/play.core. The site fonts are proprietary and licensed to ertdfgcvb.xyz only.
pricing_detail: Free to use in the browser. The core library is open source under Apache-2.0. The site fonts, Simple Console and Riforma Mono, are proprietary.
agent_guidance:
Read https://play.ertdfgcvb.xyz/llms.txt. It gives the program format, the context object, the module list and the rules. Get the example list from /src/programs/programs.json.

Write one ES module with main(coord, context) and an @author, @title and @desc header. Open it in the editor with a #/code/ link that holds the deflated, base64url source. Do not copy the site fonts.
why_it_matters: It is a small, documented way to make text-mode visuals in the browser, and each example shows its source.
tier_reason: Apache-2.0 core with 546 stars and a push on 2026-11-23, 47 example programs, and an llms.txt with the full API. Held below S because the output is text-only, which limits the use, and the fonts are not open.

name: Pressroom Poster Studio
tagline: Browser poster editor for brutalist posters and stamps, with an image generation button

The page has 18 reference layouts, an artwork library of 29 images, image upload and a stamp mode for one, two or three joined stamps. Canvas formats are 1:1, 3:4, 4:5, 9:16 and 16:9. Export gives PNG files.

name: Depthio
tagline: Free iPhone app that makes depth maps from photos on device and spins them in 3D
description:
Depthio is a free iPhone app by Sota Ono. It turns a photo into a depth map with Depth Anything 3, which runs on the device. iPhones with less memory get a lighter model. The listing says a photo takes about 6 seconds on iPhone 15 Pro.

You can view the result flat, as floating layers, or as 3D points in the photo's own colors. You can color and grade the map, add gradients, light waves, grain and dot patterns, and crop with an AI re-read of the cropped area. Exports include a 16-bit grayscale PNG depth map, a side-by-side image, videos up to 4K at 60 fps, a morph video and a PLY point cloud for Blender.

The app has no ads, no in-app purchases and no data collection. It needs iOS 26 or later, and the download is about 400 MB.
pricing_detail: Free. No ads and no in-app purchases.

This is an iPhone app with no web version and no API. Point the user to the App Store page.

name: Hitbox
tagline: Tailwind CSS 4 utilities that extend a control's click area while the content stays aligned
description:
Hitbox is a small CSS package by Marcelo Chaman for Tailwind CSS 4.1 or later. It extends the clickable area of a control with an absolutely positioned ::after element, so the layout and the alignment of the content do not change.

Classes cover all sides, each edge and each axis, for example hitbox-4, hitbox-top-4 and hitbox-x-4. A hover:hitbox: variant colors the extended area, and hitbox-center-y keeps contents centered when the top and bottom extensions differ. Edge classes override axis classes, and axis classes override the all-sides value.

The page has a live demo for each direction and a share-dialog example. The package is @regular-ppl/hitbox on npm, version 0.1.0, under MIT.
pricing_detail: Free on npm under the MIT licence.
agent_guidance:
Install with bun add -d @regular-ppl/hitbox, then add @import '@regular-ppl/hitbox'; after @import 'tailwindcss'; in the main stylesheet. It needs Tailwind CSS 4.1 or later.

Put the hitbox class on a positioned element, such as a button with relative. Read the class table on the page for the edge, axis and hover variants.
why_it_matters: It gives larger touch and click targets for small controls without padding hacks that move the layout.
tier_reason: MIT npm package with a clear class table and live demos. Held at C because it is version 0.1.0, published on 2026-11-22, and the npm entry links no source repository.
